items.title: Telangana: BRS to launch campaign against Congress government from Sept 2
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) is set to launch a week-long statewide campaign from September 2 to highlight what it describes as the failures of the Congress government in Telangana as it completes 1,000 days in office. During a teleconference on Sunday, August 23, BRS working president KT Rama Rao (KTR) alleged that the Congress had failed to deliver on the promises it made before coming to power. He said the party had announced 420 promises, 13 declarations and six guarantees, with an assurance that they would be implemented within 100 days. According to KTR, the government had not fully implemented even one of these commitments despite completing 1,000 days in office. He urged party leaders to focus not only on the unfulfilled promises but also on issues that people were currently facing. The BRS plans to hold a series of programmes during the seven-day campaign, with leaders expected to interact directly with women, farmers, youth, students, Dalits, backward classes, tribals and other communities. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently took strong exception to the State government's argument that CCTV cameras at a police station in Bengaluru were not working due to power outage and lack of back up power [V Shailaja v The Commissioner] . Justice Suraj Govindaraj said that such a stance amounted to mockery of the Supreme Court' s 2020 order to install CCTV cameras in all police stations. "Mockery of the Supreme Court order..What to do? This is a mockery of the order and you submit a report that you complied (with the Supreme Court order). There's an affidavit filed in Supreme Court that every police station has CCTV cameras, fully functional 24 hours. The only conclusion we can arrive at is that you were also happy with it not working; that is why you did not do anything for 1.5 years, it served your purpose. There is no other conclusion that we can draw," the Court remarked. The very purpose of installing CCTV cameras in police stations is defeated if the systems are allowed to remain non-functional during power outages, the bench said. Vinus Sharma ]. Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal on August 3, sought the assistance of a Senior Additional Advocate General in the matter. The case involves a question of whether the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 - which replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC) with effect from July 1, 2024 - would be applicable to a criminal complaint arising from an offence committed before the new criminal laws came into force. “ Since an important question of law has been raised in the instant matter, this Court, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, deems it appropriate to request Ms. Monika Kohli, learned Senior AAG, to render valuable assistance in the instant matter with a view to appreciate the controversy in question," the High Court said. items.title: ED searches homes of Karnataka IAS officer in KPSC exam irregularities case
items.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Sunday, August 23, searched the Bengaluru and Bareilly residences of IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar as part of its investigation into alleged irregularities in a Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) recruitment examination. Gyanendra, a 2016-batch Karnataka-cadre IAS officer from Uttar Pradesh, is currently serving as Director of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) in the Karnataka Department of Industries and Commerce. He had earlier served as Controller of Examinations at the KPSC from February 2024 to March 2026, when the recruitment examination for veterinary officers was conducted. The searches were carried out under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), according to media reports. The ED has not, however, publicly established that Gyanendra himself accepted bribes or participated in the alleged recruitment irregularities. His role as the KPSC examination controller has brought him under scrutiny in the ongoing investigation. items.title: Is this how you deal with customers? Calcutta HC to HDFC bank over blocking of Abhishek Banerjee’s account
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Thursday criticised HDFC bank for the manner in which Trinamool Congress (TMC) leader Abhishek Banerjee’s bank account was blocked [ Abhishek Banerjee v. Union of India ]. Banerjee’s counsel, Senior Advocate Ayan Bhattacharya , told the Court that the TMC leader's HDFC bank account as well as his credit and debit cards, were blocked on the same day that the Supreme Court permitted him to travel abroad for eye treatment. A communication from the bank said that the account was being temporarily suspended pending an additional due diligence exercise and that Banerjee had to visit the bank to resolve the issue, Bhattacharya added. In response to the Court’s queries, HDFC’s counsel said that certain additional KYC (Know Your Customer) related documents were required from Banerjee. Justice Krishna Rao , however, questioned why the bank had insisted on Banerjee visiting its branch merely for KYC verification. “Your bank is not on e-KYC? Your bank is very keen to see the person come personally. If the bank is interested to see the face of the client, then I will tell - if photograph will suffice. Nowadays, even the government offices are doing everything online.

items.title: ‘Putting data on a server does not make it statistically useful’
items.summary: India is preparing to revamp parts of its official statistical system, conduct at least 14 surveys under the National Sample Survey Office this year, and make better use of its administrative and digital data. But, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s ( MoSPI ) budget for 2026-27 is 22 percent below its estimated expenses, and will not be enough to meet the physical targets of its programmes, the Ministry told a Parliamentary standing committee in a report published in March 2026. On the other hand, it had surrendered Rs 6,088 crore ($711 million) over the last three financial years. For 2026-27, MoSPI estimated expenses of Rs 5,826 crore ($625 million), but allocations in the Union budget amounted to Rs 4,522 crore ($485 million) for schemes, a shortfall of about 22 percent. Of the amount allocated, 87 percent is for the Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLAD), under which each MP is provided Rs 5 crore each year to support local developmental activities.
